caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No.79 of 1995 with Civil Rule No. 186 (FM) of 1995.
lawyer:
Asrarul Hossain with HR Sharif and Joynal Abedin, Advocates — For the Appellant.
Moudud Ahmed with Md Azizul Hoq, Advocates — For the Respondent.
parties:
Mainul Hosein ------ Appellant
Vs.
Anwar Hossain Manju ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Karim J : This first Miscellaneous Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 6-4-95 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge 1st Court, Dhaka, in Arbitration Misc Case No. 49 of 1994 rejecting the prayer of the appellant-petitioner for an interim injunction under rule 4 of the Second Schedule read with section 41(b) of the Arbitration Act 1940. A Rule was issued at the instance of the appellant-petitioner calling upon the respondent-opposite party to show cause as to why an interim injunction under the provision of rule 4 of the Second Schedule read with section 41 the Arbitration Act should not be issued restraining him from spending cash of the company except by withdrawal from the bank account of the company. Both the Appeal and the Rule have been heard together and will  be disposed of by this judgment. 

 2. Facts out of which the first Miscellaneous Appeal arises, in short, are that, the Ittefaq Group of Publications Limited is a private limited company comprising petitioner Mainul Hosein, opposite party Anwar Hossain Manju, their wives, mother (since deceased) and two sisters. The management of the company was entrusted to an Executive Committee under Article 52 of the Articles of Association of the company. The Executive Committee was constituted with the petitioner as Executive Director-I and the opposite party Anwar Hossain as Executive Director-II, the powers of the Executive Directors were to be regulated by the Special Resolutions of the company. Various departments and sections of the company were put under the supervision and responsibility of each of the Executive Directors subject to the control and supervision of the Board of Directors. As per Articles of Association and also practice, the entire cash receipts of the company used to be deposited in the bank account of the company for which a Branch of Pubali Bank is operating within the premises of the Company at 1, Ramkrishna Mission Road, each of the Directors has the power to operate the bank account separately if the amount does not exceed Taka 3,000.00 and for any amount exceeding Taka 3,000.00 by joint operation by both the Directors. Mr Anwar Hossain, Executive Director-II after ceasing to hold the office of a Minister, started handling the cash without first depositing the same in the bank account and thereby spending the cash of the company for his personal gain. As this constitutes a dispute threatening a deadlock in the management of the company and also affecting the interests of the petitioner, he requested the opposite party in writing to refer the dispute in arbitration, but the latter having refused the request, the petitioner ultimately filed an application under section 20 of the Arbitration Act before the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, with a prayer that the agreement be filed and a reference be made to an arbitrator. In the meantime, an application for an interim injunction was moved before the learned Subordinate Judge, who by his order dated 6-4-95 rejected the prayer. Aggrieved by the rejection of the prayer, the petitioner has preferred the present appeal. 

 3. Mr Asrarul Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant-petitioner,submits that under Article 49(ix) of the Articles of Association it is incumbent on the Directors to open a bank account, deposit money therein and to draw cheques thereon and to transact all business in connection therewith and that Article 80 also makes it incumbent upon the directors to cause true accounts to be kept of all the assets and liabilities of the company and of all sums of money received and expended by the company. Mr Asrarul Hossain submits that under the provisions of these two articles and also the practice of the company, the Director in charge of Accounts, namely, the respondent-opposite party, is bound to deposit all sums of money received by the company into bank account before spending any amount and that the respondent-opposite party in flagrant violation of the Articles of the Association and the practice of the company has been spending money of the company for his personal gain before first depositing the same into the bank account. Mr Hossain further submits that without taking into consideration the provisions of the Articles of Association of the company and also the two special resolutions dated 26-7-71 and 31-1-71 and total disregard of the practice of the company the learned Subordinate Judge refused the prayer of the appellant petitioner for an interim injunction till disposal of Arbitration Miscellaneous case. 

 4. Mr Moudud Ahmed, learned Advocate for the respondent-opposite party has submitted that all the troubles had started from the refusal of the appellant petitioner to subscribe his signature upon the cheques for joint operation of the bank accounts, which brought the affairs of the company like payment of salary to the staff to a standstill. The Executive Director in charge of Accounts had to overcome this difficulty by making payments from cash. The affidavit-in-opposition filed on behalf of the respondent opposite party mentions that during the last 22 years the petitioner hardly took any big amount through cheques other than nominal one and that in 1992 he took from the company Taka 2 crore in cash and also about taka two crore in cash during 1993-94. Mr Moudud Ahmed submits that the internal management of the company cannot be looked into or interfered with by the court and that the Board of Directors is the appropriate forum for such matters to be taken into and decided upon. Lastly, Mr Moudud Ahmed submits that the Arbitration case under section 20 of the Arbitration Act being pending before the learned Subordinate Judge there is no prima facie case for issuance of an interim injunction and that the learned Subordinate Judge was right in refusing the prayer. 

 5. Admittedly, various departments and sections of the company were placed under the supervision of each of the Executive Directors, namely Mr Mainul Hosein (Executive Director I) and Mr Anwar Hossain Manju (Executive Director II) under the special Resolution dated 26-7-71, the company's bank account or accounts are to be operated by the Executive Directors separately when the amount does not exceed Rs 3,000.00 and under their joint signatures in case of any amount exceeding Rs 3,000.00. The special Resolution of 31-1-71 empowers the Executive Director in charge of Accounts (Mr Anwar Hossain) to sanction in addition to departmental expenses for the company expenses up to a limit of Taka 5,000.00 only in a month. 

 8. Mr Asrarul Hossain, learned Advocate for the appellant petitioner, submits that in a proceeding under section 20 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, the court has the power under section 41(b) read with rule 4 of the Second Schedule to the Act to issue an interim injunction and for this he has relied upon the decision in the case of Union of India vs Raman Iron Foundry reported in AIR 1974 (SC) 1265. Mr Moudud Ahmed has not differed as to the proposition of law, but has argued that this is not an appropriate case where rule 4 of the Second Schedule read with section 41 of the Arbitration Act applies. 

 12. We have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel of both the appellant petitioner and the respondent opposite party, perused the impugned judgment and the affidavits filed by both sides. In this judgment the learned Subordinate Judge has mentioned that since the application under section 20 of the Arbitration Act is pending between the parties there is no prima facie case for an interim injunction. In consequence, he finds no balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of issuance of an interim injunction. We are in agreement with the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that pending the conclusion of hearing of the application under section 20 of the Arbitration Act, no prima facie case is made out by the appellant petitioner. The question of balance of convenience and inconvenience does not arise at this stage.
